title: PM Modi, Putin share car ride in Delhi, weeks after traveling together in Bishkek - watch
content: During an informal car ride in Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin rekindled their camaraderie, continuing their tradition of traveling together. This ride marks their fourth time sharing a vehicle, following earlier occasions in Bishkek and Tianjin. Their private talks during the journey underscore the depth of their diplomatic ties and mutual understanding.

title: Putin brings 'Flying Kremlin' to India for Brics: What makes 'Doomsday Plane' different?
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi for a summit and bilateral talks. He traveled on a specially modified Ilyushin IL-96-300PU aircraft for security. This aircraft functions as a mobile command center with advanced communication systems. The United States operates comparable aircraft for its own national command needs. These planes are designed for survivability during national emergencies and conflicts.

title: Aadhaar Card global push: UIDAI working on access for NRIs and OCIs
content: Speaking during a fireside chat at Global Fintech Fest 2026, UIDAI CEO Saurabh Vijay said his objective is to build Aadhaar into a best-in-class digital identity infrastructure that can support its expansion internationally.

title: Elon Musk's Cybercab rollout puts US safety rules to test as NHTSA audits 1,000 cars
content: Tesla's new Cybercab robotaxis are now operating in Texas without traditional controls. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an audit of these vehicles. US safety regulations were primarily designed for human-driven cars. Tesla's strategy relies on self-driving software and robotics for its valuation. Experts suggest Tesla may challenge regulatory interpretations to deploy its vehicles.

title: ‘He rejected it’: Ex-PCB selector blames Imran Khan for Pakistan cricket’s downfall
content: Former chief selector of Pakistan cricket, Haroon Rasheed, identifies the setbacks in the sport to Imran Khan's reforms. Rasheed highlighted that Khan dismissed a hybrid model for the domestic cricket structure, significantly diminishing the first-class teams in Pakistan. He pointed out that India's layered domestic system promotes talent depth, advocating for Pakistan to decentralise its cricket governance to enhance the game.

title: 'I don't want to be murdered by a Chinese robot'
content: Hopefully, whatever version of doomsday the AI world is worried about waits until after Avengers: Doomsday, because after all the multiverse nonsense and speculation about how Robert Downey Jr is going to return to the MCU as Doctor Doom, one really wants to watch Kevin Feige explain that before artificial intelligence kills everyone.

title: Countries where you can buy iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max cheaper than India
content: Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models have officially launched worldwide.  These devices feature the powerful A20 Pro chip and improved camera technology.  Pricing for these flagship iPhones varies considerably across different countries.  The United States offers the most affordable purchase option for both models.  India's pricing reflects higher local taxes and import duties on electronics.

title: 112 years later! Robinson enters rarest Test bowling club with sub-19 average
content: In a remarkable feat, Ollie Robinson has achieved a bowling average of under nineteen after his 20th match, making him the first bowler to do so since the iconic Sydney Barnes in 1914. With two crucial wickets during Pakistan's second innings at Edgbaston, Robinson joins a select group of five bowlers with this outstanding record, positioning himself among the top wicket-takers in cricket history.

title: GPS collars revealed male lions follow hyenas, not the other way around
content: A groundbreaking study suggests that it's the male lions that approach spotted hyenas, contrary to the belief that hyenas seek out lion remains for food. In fact, spotted hyenas are known to back away from lions, prioritizing their safety. This finding highlights the importance of spatial avoidance in hyena behavior, emphasizing their adaptive strategies to circumvent confrontations with such powerful hunters.

title: Instead of managing billions, Warren Buffett’s son Howard Buffett chose farming
content: Choosing a path less traveled, Howard Buffett, the son of Warren Buffett, dedicated his life to farming and conservation rather than finance. He skillfully managed farms in Nebraska and Illinois, prioritizing soil health. Warren Buffett supported his passion by purchasing a Nebraska farm for his son. As he transitions to the role of non-executive chairman at Berkshire Hathaway, Howard aims to safeguard the company’s culture following his father's legacy.

title: Putin invites PM Modi to Russia for 24th annual summit - key points from Brics summit
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Russian President Vladimir Putin during the summit.  Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also arrived for discussions with PM Modi.  Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected for bilateral talks and the summit.  The expanded Brics grouping focuses on development and cooperation among emerging economies.  India hosts the summit under its theme of resilience and innovation.

title: France sends Rafales on 40,000-km global mission to project power from Arctic to Indo-Pacific
content: The Pegase 26 mission from France brings Rafale jets into action as they journey 40,000 kilometers across three continents. This ambitious undertaking not only demonstrates France's skills in executing swift long-distance operations but also enhances collaborative capabilities with partners through essential aerial refueling. Taking an innovative northern route crossing the Arctic, the mission underscores France's strategic prominence and dedication to bolstering global security relationships.

title: Bihar’s Vas Sthal Kray Sahayata scheme: Rs 60,000 aid for landless families; key provisions explained
content: The Mukhyamantri Vas Sthal Kray Sahayata Yojana in Bihar is designed to assist landless families by providing Rs 60,000. This financial aid is specifically for those eligible for the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin to buy residential plots. The program is aimed at villages lacking government land for housing, ensuring funds are directly deposited into beneficiaries' bank accounts after thorough verification.

title: Patrick Mahomes injury: Why is the Chiefs star frustrated by knee doubts?
content: Patrick Mahomes is growing frustrated with repeated questions about his knee injury as he prepares for the Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 1 opener against the Denver Broncos. After suffering ACL and LCL tears last December, Mahomes has worked toward a nine-month recovery. He made his desire to move past the injury discussion clear, while head coach Andy Reid offered encouraging news by saying Mahomes is most likely to start.

title: LeBron James and Savannah James: Why did they keep Zhuri away from the spotlight?
content: LeBron and Savannah James made a thoughtful decision to shield their daughter Zhuri from the spotlight for several years, aiming to protect her early years from relentless media attention. Her first public appearance was a natural moment during LeBron's championship celebration in 2016, allowing her to cultivate her own passions independent of basketball. The family emphasized the importance of privacy and personal growth for each of their children.

title: After Pakistan's cybercrime summons, Rizwan & Imam face domestic cricket setback
content: Following their recent tour in England, Pakistani cricketers Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq find themselves under scrutiny due to a cybercrime investigation triggered by evidence from their mobile phones. As a result of their inability to meet fitness requirements, both players will miss the opening round of the President's Trophy Grade-I, amid the aftermath of a challenging tour filled with recalls.

title: PM Modi's special gift to Putin comes with a Tamil connection
content: During a significant meeting ahead of the BRICS Summit, Prime Minister Modi gifted President Putin a translated version of the ancient Tamil text, Thirukkural, by Naira Mkrtchyan. Both leaders held bilateral talks on the sidelines of the Brics summit being held in New Delhi.

title: Powerful explosion in TMC leader's house in Bengal; BJP claims bombs stored inside
content: A large explosion severely damaged a house in Baruipur, South 24 Parganas. Police suspect a gas cylinder caused the blast, while locals allege bomb storage. The house belonged to Dwijen Mondal, who has not been seen recently. No casualties were reported from the significant structural damage. An investigation is ongoing to determine the exact cause of the explosion.

title: Maaya Rajeshwaran, Sushkova stun 4th seeds to storm into US Open junior semis
content: Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi and Antonina Sushkova secured a significant victory in New York.The Indo-Ukrainian pair defeated the fourth-seeded Russian team in straight sets.They demonstrated strong serving and saved crucial break points during the match.This win follows their earlier upset against the fifth seeds in the second round.Next, the duo will face American twins Kristina and Annika Penickova in the semi-finals.

title: UPI now dominates merchant payments: Are cards becoming less useful?
content: UPI now dominates Indian merchant payments, significantly reducing card usage. Debit cards are primarily used for cash withdrawals, not shopping. Credit cards are specializing in larger purchases and e-commerce transactions. RuPay credit cards can now link directly to UPI apps. The QR code scan is becoming the default checkout method for everyday purchases.

title: 'Double-edged sword': Sitharaman flags AI risks, urges efficiency without fragility
content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman addressed artificial intelligence risks at the Global Fintech Fest 2026. She highlighted technology's potential to influence public opinion and electoral outcomes. The Reserve Bank of India recognized the Unified Fintech Forum as a self-regulatory organization. Sitharaman emphasized balancing innovation with necessary risk mitigation measures. India's young population is driving innovation and economic growth, she stated.

title: Houthis take control of island in Bab el-Mandeb Strait; vital trade artery at risk
content: In a strategic move, Houthi forces have seized the port city of Mocha and are pushing further south towards the crucial Bab el-Mandeb Strait. This escalation shifts their tactics toward controlling Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital route for global maritime trade connecting Asia with Europe. As tensions rise, the humanitarian situation in Yemen worsens, prompting urgent international calls for intervention to address the impending crisis.

title: 10 days, 1,981 runs, no winner: ENG vs SA Test that ended with a ship to catch
content: In 1939, England and South Africa played a "Timeless Test" match without any time limit. South Africa batted for nearly three days, scoring 530 runs in their first innings. England replied with 316 runs, and South Africa then added 481 more. England chased a massive 696-run target, reaching 654/5 after ten days of play.

title: A ‘beer party’ trap: Man kills friend with iron rod over suspected affair with wife

Police claim Praveen alias Papla murdered Jitender due to suspicion of an affair with his wife. Praveen and his nephew Aman Kumar were apprehended by the authorities. The accused are now in police custody for further investigation and evidence recovery.

title: Red alert in Delhi after heavy rain lashes parts of city
content: Heavy rain lashed parts of Delhi on Friday as a red alert was issued. Moderate to heavy rainfall is forecast for many areas of the city. Light to moderate rain may also occur in the evening hours. Rainfall activity is expected to continue over Delhi for two days. The weather office issued the alert for the next few hours.

Akram also stressed the need to strengthen cricket at the grassroots level. He called for greater focus on club, school and college cricket to ensure a steady supply of talent.

title: No-stop toll plazas by March 2027? Nitin Gadkari sets deadline for barrier-free system
content: India is set to roll out a barrier-free digital tolling system by early 2027, allowing vehicles to glide past toll booths without stopping. The integration of number-plate recognition with existing FASTag technology promises to streamline the toll collection process even further. Motorists will experience a new level of convenience as the One Tag system is introduced, significantly reducing wait times and enhancing overall travel efficiency.

title: Terror groups, China turn to off-the-shelf AI to make weapons smarter
content: Anthropic revealed state actors used AI for weapons development and intelligence.  A China-based actor built electronic warfare software targeting Taiwan's defenses.  Yemen-based actors developed guided rockets and ballistic missiles using AI.  These AI-enabled threats impact regional security and shipping lanes.  Indian planners must consider these evolving state and non-state AI threats.

title: Delhi man goes for infertility test, finds out he has uterus
content: A 26-year-old man seeking infertility treatment discovered a rare congenital condition.  He had a uterus and fallopian-tube-like structures inside his body.  Doctors also found undescended testes with severe damage and pre-cancerous changes.  Minimally invasive surgery removed these structures and the damaged testes.  The case highlights the importance of investigating unexplained infertility and undescended testes.

title: 'Smashed heads with stone': Man kills wife, 3 daughters in Jaipur
content: A man allegedly killed his wife and three daughters in Jaipur's Kardhani area. He reportedly used a stone to strike them on their heads while they slept. The accused then collected milk from a deliveryman before fleeing the scene. Police are searching for the suspect and investigating a possible family dispute. The victims were found at their home in Govind Vatika early Friday morning.

title: Elon Musk feels 'chess will be fully solved one day'; what does Carlsen think?
content: Elon Musk believes chess will eventually be fully solved by AI, drawing comparisons with checkers. Magnus Carlsen was less certain, saying he isn't a computer expert but noting chess is already “semi-solved” as a likely draw. Carlsen also praised AI for making chess more accessible, while backing the Global Chess League’s exciting team format and enjoying his visits to India.

title: 'My name was not even in the FIR': Former India cricketer’s 22-year ordeal

The court's ruling highlighted the absence of credible evidence against Martin, allowing him to close this challenging chapter of his life and career. He can now look forward to a brighter future, free from the shadows of this protracted legal battle.

content: three students at Universiti Malaya have built a prototype to recover electricity from water flowing down the sink . the micro-hydropower system is designed specifically for the weak and intermittent flow produced by household wastewater . it filters and temporarily stores the water before releasing it through a nozzle at higher speed .

title: JPC meet on FCRA Bill: Panel to hold first sitting on Sept 18
content: the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, will hold its first meeting in parliament on sept 18 . the 31-member committee was constituted after the Centre moved a motion in Parliament to refer the FCRA Amendment Bill to a JPC .

title: Indian-origin taxi driver drove New Yorkers for free for 40 days after 9/11
content: shabbos Kestenbaum shared the story on X, saying his taxi driver, Gurvinder Singh, told him he was at the world trade center on the morning of September 11, 2001 . Singh continued helping New Yorkers afterward by giving rides to those who needed them and refusing payment .

title: Cong vs Cong over Brics: Tharoor rebuffs Chidambaram, hails 'power' of summit
content: senior Congress leader says the expanded Brics grouping represents a significant share of the global population and economy . Tharoor says it gives India a platform to engage with the Global South and a “diplomatic convening power” .

title: Full list of world leaders attending Brics summit in New Delhi
content: the stage is set for the 18th h Brics summit in new Delhi from 12-13 . leaders discuss global governance, multilateralism, and the ongoing conflicts in west Asia and Ukraine . the summit kickstarts on Saturday, with a closed-door meeting of member countries at 2.35 pm .
